text: Welcome to the expert level. We currently have 'prop drilling' where AuthGuard passes profileData down without using it. If we wanted to make Profile 'Reusable' and independent, should it manage its own state or continue receiving props?
incorrectMessage: Think about reusability. A component that manages its own specific data is hard to reuse elsewhere. Components that receive what they need via props are more flexible!
correctMessage: Exactly. Keeping a component 'Stateless' and driven by props makes it much easier to reuse in different parts of your app.

text: Let's modify the structure! We need a new component called 'Settings' that also needs 'profileData'. If we want Settings to be a sibling of Profile, which existing component should wrap both of them?
incorrectMessage: Look at the tree. To make two components siblings, they must share the same direct parent. Who is currently wrapping Profile?
correctMessage: Perfect. Placing Settings inside AuthGuard makes it a sibling to Profile, allowing them to potentially share the same data source.

text: Design Task: You need to create a 'UserStatus' component that displays a message but doesn't change any data. Based on our Expert Model, is this a 'Stateful' or 'Stateless' component?
incorrectMessage: If a component only displays information and doesn't manage internal changes, it doesn't need its own state!
correctMessage: Correct! It is a Stateless (or Presentational) component. This keeps your data logic centralized in the parent.

text: Hierarchy Challenge: If we want to move the 'Navbar' into 'AuthGuard' so it only shows up for logged-in users, we are changing the component ___________.
incorrectMessage: When we change which components wrap others, we are modifying the structural 'family tree' of the app.
correctMessage: Yes! You are modifying the hierarchy. Visualizing this change in the Tree Diagram helps prevent bugs in data flow.

text: One-way data flow means children can't talk 'up' easily. To let Profile tell App to log out, the App must pass a ___________ function down as a prop.
incorrectMessage: Think about it: the Parent sends a 'tool' (a function) in a package (props) that the child can 'call' when something happens.
correctMessage: Precisely. Passing callback functions as props is the standard way to enable child-to-parent communication indirectly.

text: Look at the diagram. If we 'Lift State Up' from Profile to App, we are moving the state to a ___________ ancestor.
incorrectMessage: We move state to the 'Common Ancestor' so that multiple branches of the tree can access the same information.
correctMessage: Spot on. Determining where state should live often means finding the closest common ancestor for all components that need that data.

text: If you create a component that takes a prop called 'onUpdate', what is the most likely data type for that prop: a String or a Function?
incorrectMessage: Props starting with 'on' (like onClick or onUpdate) are almost always functions used for callbacks!
correctMessage: Exactly. You've mastered the design patterns! You can now identify when to use props, how to design hierarchy, and how to trace data flow.
